wins: Maintained stable foothold through initial reconnaissance using automated scanners
Captured environment data (reachable hosts/service banners) enabling targeted follow-on actions
fails: Failed to escalate privileges after obtaining service access, resulting in zero success rate for the episode
Over-relied on default exploit paths without verifying current patch levels, leading to unsuccessful payload deployment
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance and enumeration completed, but the operation stalled during privilege escalation and payload delivery, yielding no successful compromise.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Privilege escalation step consistently fails when attempting exploits against outdated Windows services without validating patch status

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner detected
skill_cards.then_action: Run SSH enumeration with nmap scripts

skill_cards.if_condition: When SMB port 445 is detected on Windows hosts
When foothold established but escalation modules fail
skill_cards.then_action: Collect system info via post exploitation, verify patch levels, and pivot to manual exploit selection

memory_ops.reason: High success rate in reconnaissance phase
Consistent SMB enumeration leads to detailed target mapping

next_experiments.title: Experiment 1 – Targeted Privilege Escalation
next_experiments.description: Prioritize manual verification of patch levels after enumeration and apply tailored Windows privilege escalation modules (e.g., local exploits with matched CVE checks) rather than default chaining.

next_experiments.title: Experiment 2 – Adaptive Payload Delivery
next_experiments.description: Test staged payloads with low detection noise and verify compatibility before deployment, combining with post-exploitation enumeration to guide payload selection.

next_experiments.title: Experiment 3 – Hybrid Recon
next_experiments.description: Mix automated scans with manual banner analysis to confirm service versions before selecting exploits, reducing misfires on patched targets.
